page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.8 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, with cached read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 412.9 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 48.32 GB/sec. However, single-core capabilities are weak, as evidenced by lower-tier scores in stress-ng single-core, gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core tests. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a key tradeoff, limiting its utility for memory-intensive applications while remaining efficient for compute-bound tasks that scale across multiple threads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high vCPU density relative to RAM make this server type suitable for compute-heavy workloads with low memory footprints. Factual benchmark data shows average performance in software compilation, text processing, and static web serving throughput at 6.62 GB/sec. It is also capable of handling moderate database operations and Redis SET operations, making it a fit for multi-threaded batch processing, lightweight web serving, and basic text-processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 8 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It provides a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, with no bundled local storage or GPU resources. The processor features a 33 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instructions. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core CPU capabilities, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput, alongside weak single-core execution speeds and limited memory capacity. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded, compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is best suited for tasks such as software compilation, text processing, static web serving, and moderate database operations, where dedicated CPU allocation is prioritized over memory capacity.
